lesson.child_mission: 12-hour time uses am/pm; 24-hour time counts hours from 00 to 23 so afternoon times continue past 12.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same method to a larger number or a new context, then compare two solution paths for accuracy.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Convert 4:15 pm to 24-hour time and 19:40 to 12-hour time with am/pm.

FEEDBACK
16:15; 7:40 pm.

WATCH FOR
Treating 15:00 as 5:00 pm (subtracting 10 instead of 12) misreads afternoon time.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Convert twenty times both ways (12↔24 hour). Explain the am/pm decision for six.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: 12-hour time uses am/pm; 24-hour time counts hours from 00 to 23 so afternoon times continue past 12.
materials: Optional: place-value chart or number line
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Convert twenty times both ways (12↔24 hour). Explain the am/pm decision for six. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: 16:15; 7:40 pm. Reasoning: I used 12-hour by attending to 24-hour rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Treating 15:00 as 5:00 pm (subtracting 10 instead of 12) misreads afternoon time. Correction: 16:15; 7:40 pm. Why: the correction restores accurate use of 12-hour.

Parent: Likely misconception: Treating 15:00 as 5:00 pm (subtracting 10 instead of 12) misreads afternoon time. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Solve one fresh problem that uses 12-hour with different numbers from the worked model. Show working and name the places or values that matter.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Describe one likely mistake with 12-hour, show corrected working, and say why the correction works.

Parent: Marking notes: Require new numbers, visible working and named places/values. / Require a real misconception, corrected working and a method reason..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
3:00 pm = 15:00. 7:30 am = 07:30. Midnight 00:00; noon 12:00. Add 12 hours to pm times (except 12 pm stays 12).

TRY FIRST
Convert 4:15 pm to 24-hour time and 19:40 to 12-hour time with am/pm.

FEEDBACK
16:15; 7:40 pm.
teach_steps.explain:
12-hour time uses am/pm; 24-hour time counts hours from 00 to 23 so afternoon times continue past 12.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Treating 15:00 as 5:00 pm (subtracting 10 instead of 12) misreads afternoon time. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
